_source: shared_knowledge/docs/content-voice-style-guide-playbook.md §3 — that document is the human-readable authority; this file is its machine-readable form. Change the playbook first, then mirror it here.

phrases._comment: §3a BANNED WORDS & PHRASES. Matched case-insensitively on word boundaries. `skipInQuotes` honours §3c: a banned word inside a direct quotation or a proper name is allowed.
hedge: at the end of the day
phrases._newComment: 2026-10-11 (no-ai-slop gap closure). The four lists below are WARN ONLY — they never fail a gate. Deliberately left OUT because they are legitimate words: robust, tapestry, harness, realm, foster, beacon (analytics beacon), intricate (architectural description) - both review-only, overall (only the comma-openers "Overall," and "Ultimately," are listed, and only when they OPEN A PARAGRAPH; "Overall difficulty is mild" is fine), just/simply/actually/truly/literally (per-hit).

structure._comment: §3b BANNED AI STRUCTURAL PATTERNS as measurable thresholds. minBurstiness is the standard deviation of sentence word-count. Treat it as a READABILITY floor, not an AI detector: research shows perplexity/burstiness cannot reliably separate human from machine text, and ordinary reference prose often scores 'AI-like'. Monotonous rhythm is still bad writing, which is why it stays an error.
structure._crutchComment: Advisory only (warn). Added 2026-10-05 after a content audit: the ban-list was clean but 'genuinely' and 'honest(ly)' appeared on most pages — constant claims of honesty are themselves a machine tell. Warns when the combined rate exceeds the max per 1,000 words.
structure._newComment: 2026-10-11: uniformSentences is an ERROR only at >= uniformSentencesErrorMinWords words; below that it is a WARN (an honest 86-word, 10-sentence spa paragraph scored sd 3.98 and was blocked; raising minSentences to 8 would not have fixed it). structureChecksMinWords gates the regex structure checks (binary contrast, negative listing, trailing -ing clause, colon reveal, fragments, emoji heading), all WARN only.

disclosure._comment: Not a style rule — a hard product rule. Sounding human is craft; CLAIMING to be human when directly asked is deception, and for an interactive assistant it is also an EU AI Act Art. 50 transparency issue. Guest-facing bots must answer this honestly.
